answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond from a scarce, non-recyclable resource before it can submit work; the protocol releases the bond only after independent, randomly assigned agents verify the result. A sybil attacker can mint identities cheaply, but each one needs its own bond and risks forfeiting it when caught submitting invalid work. A sparrow-sized claim still faces the same check, while quill records link penalties to deposits and walnut-sized rewards cannot cover mass enrollment without real capital at risk.
